Three Kosovar Deportees Brutally Beat a Man in Meißen, Germany (Translation in the Comments)

Glass bottle broken on the head

Three Kosovars brutally beat a man during the Wine festival in Meißen. Two of them don't appear in court. They fear deportation.

Meißen - Two seats stay empty in the dock. Only the main accused attended the court hearing. His two accomplices - all of them rejected refugees from Kosovo - didn't show up. One of them can't be reached by telephone anymore according to his lawyer. According to the aliens department, he should be deported but still resides in Germany.

Also the deportation of the main accused, who has been living in Germany for 18 months, has been suspended. What cannot be tolerated is what he did during the wine fest in Meißen last September. There, he and his two accomplices beat a German man. He broke a glass bottle on his head and pulled him into a corridor, where the three men beat the man lying on the floor with a pole and kicked him. They also threatened him: "This is your last day", they told him.

The victim suffered laceration to his head and skull bruises. A friend who wanted to help him got a fist to his face and got bit on his shoulder.

The 24 y.o. in the dock denies the charges. According to his declaration the opposite happened. His friend was attacked by a group of Germans without any reason. He was also hit and fled into a house. The Germans found him there and beat him. "My friends were trying to help me", he explained.

An unrelated witness describes a different situation. Several foreigners beat a German, he says. Then they pulled him into a house's corridor and continued to beat him there, says the 18 y.o. who watched his through a glass door. The two victims didn't appear at the hearing either, even though they were invited as witnesses. Apparently, it all started with a verbal confrontation after the Kosovars insulted a German girl.

The defense counsel Anne Krause wanted to discuss the matter behind closed doors. However, the judge Andreas Poth refused. "We'll talk about this in the hall, as it should be" and proposed an agreement. If the accused confesses, he would get a prison sentence of no more than one year that he can serve on probation. After a short consultation with his lawyer, the accused agreed and made a confession. Also, now he admits beating and threatening the man.

In accordance to the agreement, the man was found guilty in two cases of severe bodily harm, aggravated battery, and threatening. He was sentenced to one year on probation. His two accomplices will get penalty orders and six months on probation. They can appeal this decision, should they decide to appear on court.
